title: The Survey Team
subtitle: Residents block a land survey they believe is the first step to eviction
coldOpen: 07:00. A survey team arrives at the old settlement.
07:30. Residents surround them and pull out the markers.
A notice nobody has seen is said to be “the eviction order”.

briefing.grievance: Residents of a forty-year-old settlement believe the survey is the first step to taking their homes. They want to see the order and to be part of whatever the survey is for.
knownFacts: The survey was ordered to map the drainage line for a flood scheme.
The settlement has 300 homes; most have utility bills in their names going back decades.
No eviction order exists in the records office.
unverifiedClaims: A post shows a “demolition map” with the settlement shaded red.
A message says bulldozers are parked at the depot for tomorrow.
briefing.responsibility: You run the records office and the survey. The drainage scheme is real; so is the fear, and a map nobody explained caused it.
briefing.objective: Explain the survey, show there is no eviction order, protect the records, and finish the drainage map with residents involved.

rightsMoments.question: A drainage scheme needs two metres from two homes whose owners refuse. What does the law require?

options.text: Notice, a hearing, compensation and the least intrusive design; residents cannot be pressured through essential services.
options.feedback: Correct. Property and shelter are taken, if at all, through due process and compensation, never through collective pressure.

options.text: The scheme serves everyone, so the setback can be taken immediately.
options.feedback: Public purpose does not remove the requirement of notice, hearing and compensation.

options.text: Nothing can be done if the owners refuse.
options.feedback: Lawful acquisition with process and compensation remains possible; refusal is answered by procedure, not by force or by giving up.

rightsMoments.principle: Deprivation of property or shelter requires authority of law, due process and compensation (Articles 21 and 300A). Essential services cannot be withheld as leverage.
rightsMoments.why: Two hearings and a half-metre shift of the drain line did what a Monday demolition never could.

source.label: Constitution of India, Articles 21 and 22 (India Code)

simple.question: A drain needs two metres from two homes. The owners refuse. What does the law say?

options.a: Notice, a hearing, payment, and the gentlest design. Never pressure through power or water.
options.b: The drain helps everyone, so take the land now.
options.c: Nothing can be done if they refuse.

feedback.a: Yes! Fair steps and payment, never pressure.
feedback.b: No. Helping everyone does not skip fair steps.
feedback.c: Fair steps still exist. Refusal is answered by process, not force.

simple.principle: Land or homes can only be taken by law, with notice, a hearing and payment. Never by cutting power or water.
simple.why: Two hearings and a small shift of the drain line did what a demolition never could.

closing.good: The surveyors came back with residents holding the tape, the file left the basement as three hundred certified copies, and the drain moved half a metre to save two walls.

closing.poor: The survey was forced through, the file got wet, and the settlement now has a demolition date instead of a drain.
